title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
description: We introduce Kumo Tabular, a family of open tabular foundation models for classification and regression, in three sizes: Kumo Tabular-S (27M parameters), Kumo Tabular-M (61M), and Kumo Tabular-L (214M). Pretrained only on artificial tables from the Kumo prior, they can make predictions on new tables without any training. In our approach, a table encoder compresses each row into an embedding, and an in-context learning transformer predicts the unlabeled rows from the labeled ones. Kumo Tabular introduces architectural innovations that improve both training stability and predictive performance, enabling the model to scale up to 150M cells on modern GPUs. Kumo Tabular-L ranks first on eight benchmarks: TabArena, TALENT, BeyondArena, ScoringBench, STRABLE, MulTaBench, RamanBench, and TabBench-Bio. These cover probabilistic regression, tables with over 1M rows or 100K columns, and tables with strings, text, or images. Accuracy improves with model size in all tested comparisons. All three sizes lie on the accuracy-speed frontiers of TabArena and BeyondArena. Kumo Tabular-L predicts faster than the runners-up, LimiX-2 on TabArena (36 times) and TabPFN-3.5 on BeyondArena (1.7 times). Weights and pretraining code are released under OpenMDW-1.1 and Apache 2.0, respectively.
author: Jingang Qu, Valter Hudovernik, Martin Jurkovič, Cedric Lorenz, David Holzmüller

title: Aliyah Belwyn [LORA/SDXL 1.0]
description:
This LoRA does not depict a real person; it is a fictional creation.

Aliyah Belwyn belongs to the Belgian Belwyn family of Bruges, where music is how the house speaks when words feel too small. 🎶✨ Gilded frames, late dinners, and the expectation that beauty should take its time sat beside her from childhood. A single string, she learned, can persuade a room that was determined to talk. Candlelight still feels like the honest hour. The canals go quiet just as the salons begin, which suits her perfectly. 🥰👑

She is a concert harpist. The performances happen in gilded salons, in flowing ivory gowns and pearls, at a carved wooden harp set in oak-paneled music rooms. 🎹🕯️ She works an arpeggio until it sounds like water finding a path down marble. The audience is asked, by the simple fact of the sound, to stay inside the weather she builds. Virtuosity matters less to her than a phrase people are willing to inhabit. 💫🎻 She listens for the cough that means someone forgot the room

A Krea 2 style LoRA trained on panels from Hip Hop Family Tree by Ed Piskor, published by Fantagraphics from 2013.

About the comic

Piskor's history of hip hop starts in the Bronx in the 1970s and follows DJs, MCs, b-boys, graffiti writers, producers and labels year by year as the music spreads from block parties to the charts. He drew it as an homage to the Marvel comics of the era, down to the off-register printing, yellowed newsprint paper and Ben-Day dots. The series won an Eisner Award in 2015. Piskor died in 2023. Please look for the books.

What this LoRA does

HpHpFmTrStl gives Piskor's look: chunky black ink with heavy hatching, warm faded colours on aged paper, halftone dots, expressive faces and plenty of period detail.
